measurement_environment.java:
openjdk version "21.0.13" 2026-10-20
OpenJDK Runtime Environment (build 21.0.13+9-1-deb13u2-Debian)
OpenJDK 64-Bit Server VM (build 21.0.13+9-1-deb13u2-Debian, mixed mode, sharing)

benchmark.normalization: For each paired fork: (candidate JNI ns / candidate Java ns) / (baseline JNI ns / baseline Java ns). Report median of five paired ratios. This is a descriptive control adjustment, not a statistical confidence interval.
benchmark.tiny_shape_caveat: 1x1x1 and 256x1x1 have normalized medians 1.037 and 1.057; no kernel speedup claim for those shapes.

prior_wrapper_attempt.reason: First baseline JVM exited zero, but a perfdata lock warning preceded CSV header and wrapper parsing rejected it. Both accepted lanes then used -XX:-UsePerfData; exact header parsing fixed. Original attempt retained in scratch.

limitations: Shared Linux x86_64 environment; no exclusive hardware reservation or frequency lock
128MiB fixed heap in both lanes; same existing JVM bytecode and JNI boundary
Alternated baseline/candidate fork order, five pairs; within-fork seven alternating lane rounds
Existing harness warms for 200ms per shape and uses median per lane; bounded observation only
All shape input/output roots match across all ten runs
No automatic threshold or Java default change is justified by this experiment
Unchanged Java control lanes show substantial host/JIT variability; small-shape improvements are not attributed confidently to the kernel change

dispatch_decision: Java remains default; explicit JNI opt-in is preserved.
scope: Historical local paired measurement of the exact canonical kernel adapted into this recipient; separate emitted-product tests and handoff evidence qualify delivery. No whole-model, installed-JDK, all-platform or universal speedup claim.
preserved_observation: BENCHMARK_OBSERVATION.json remains unchanged as the preceding kernel observation.
